title: Static-deps directionality bug — test→source edges instead of source→test
description:
## Impact

The `static-deps` command in the Python adapter records edges FROM test files TO the source files they import (test→source). Selection needs the reverse: given a changed source file, find tests that depend on it (source→test). 

## Root cause

In `adapter-python.rs`, `cmd_static_deps` does `tests_by_file.get(file)` which only returns results when the changed file IS itself a test file. If `src/cositos/model.py` is changed, `get()` returns None and no edges are created. The engine falls back to "run all tests."

## Reproduction

```bash
echo -e "\n# new function\ndef new_helper(): pass" >> src/cositos/model.py
git diff > /tmp/change.diff
testaruda select --diff /tmp/change.diff
# Expected: tests/test_model.py only
# Actual: all 119 tests (could not narrow down)
```

## Location

`adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_static_deps` function

## Action

Reverse the lookup direction: for each changed source file, find all test files that import from it. Two approaches:
1. Build full import graph at discover time (preferred — more scalable)
2. Reverse lookup at select time (lighter upfront, slower per selection)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a source file is changed, `select` returns only tests that import from that source
- [ ] Python adapter creates correct source→test edges
- [ ] Existing test suite passes
- [ ] Test project (cositos) shows correct selection results

## Discovery

Found via testaruda usage report on cositos project (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-001.
acceptance_criteria: When a source file is changed, select returns only tests that import from that source. Python adapter creates correct source->test edges. Verify with: cargo test --test integration_static_deps. Existing test suite passes. Test project (cositos) shows correct selection results: testaruda select --files src/cositos/model.py --pre-edit only shows test_model.py.
notes: Spec reference: TIA-ADAPT-005 — static-deps must return candidate tests and K-valued edges for changed source files. Current implementation violates this by recording test→source instead of source→test.
close_reason: Fixed: reversed static-deps lookup direction. Changed from 'find tests at same path as changed file' to 'find test files that import from the changed source file.' 9 new tests, all 106 pass. PR a790e6c.

title: bug: adapter handshake envelope mismatch blocks all adapter communication
description: AdapterIO::spawn expects Handshake fields (name/version/protocol) at the JSON top level, but both adapter binaries wrap every response in {"ok": true, "result": {...}}. This is the only response type in the adapter protocol that omits the result wrapper. Blocks discover/static-deps/fingerprint/run-args/ingest for every configured adapter. See docs/evaluations/testaruda-evaluation.md §9.2 (I11)
acceptance_criteria: Handshake struct matches the actual wire format (enveloped like every other response)
close_reason: Handshake now deserializes through response envelope — all 88 tests pass, wire format matches real adapter output

title: Adapter pipeline only processes changed files, never full project tree
description:
## Impact

The `select` command's `run_adapter_pipeline` iterates only over the **changed files** in the delta, not the full project tree. This means:
- The adapter is spawned only when a changed file matches its extension
- Static-deps runs only on those changed files
- Test files NOT in the change set never have their import edges recorded
- The store's dependency graph is always incomplete → selection always falls back to "run all"

## Root cause

In `main.rs`, `run_adapter_pipeline` iterates `delta.files` (the changed set) instead of the full project tree. Since static-deps only processes the files it receives, most test files never get their import dependencies recorded.

## Location
- `main.rs` — `run_adapter_pipeline` function

## Action

`run_adapter_pipeline` should also run discover + static-deps on the full project tree on first invocation (or cache results of a prior `discover` pass), not just on the changed file set.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Full project tree is processed for dependency edges at least once
- [ ] Results are cached/persisted for subsequent selections
- [ ] No unnecessary re-processing on repeated invocations
- [ ] selection works correctly on first invocation

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report on cositos (2026-07-14) — Section 2c.
acceptance_criteria: On first invocation, full project tree is processed before selection is computed. Subsequent invocations use cached results for unchanged files. Using testaruda select --diff on a single changed file returns only tests that import from that file (not all tests). Cargo test passes.
close_reason: Rewrote run_adapter_pipeline to walk full project tree and run discover + static-deps on ALL files, not just changed files. All 107 tests pass. PR 7f78507.

title: Adapter discover walks into .venv — 98 of 119 tests from vendored deps
description:
## Impact

The Python adapter's discover command walks `"."` with no ignore filters, picking up every `test_*.py` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`. On cositos, 98 out of 119 discovered tests come from vendored dependencies (jsonschema, mypy, tornado, etc.).

## Root cause

`adapter-python.rs` `cmd_discover` uses `walkdir::WalkDir::new(".")` with no exclusion patterns. The engine-level `run_discover_pipeline` in `main.rs` filters `target`, `.git`, and `node_modules`, but `.venv` is not in that list.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /path/to/python/project
testaruda discover
# Output: "python-adapter discovered 119 test items"
# Expected: ~21 (project tests only)
```

## Location
- `adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_discover`
- `main.rs` — `run_discover_pipeline`

## Action
Add exclusion patterns: `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `build/`, `dist/` to adapter-level discover walk, or pass ignore list from engine config.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Python adapter discover excludes `.venv` and common cache/build directories
- [ ] Only project tests are discovered
- [ ] Configurable exclusion list in `testaruda.toml`

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-003.
acceptance_criteria: Python adapter discover excludes .venv, venv, __pycache__, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, build/, dist/. Only project tests are discovered.
notes: Spec reference: TIA-ADAPT-004 — discover SHALL enumerate test items in scope; .venv vendored tests are out of scope. Engine-level exclusion list in run_discover_pipeline (main.rs) also missing .venv.
close_reason: Fixed: added filter_entry to cmd_discover excluding .venv, __pycache__, and 9 other common dirs. Also synced to engine-level run_discover_pipeline. 2 new tests, 108 total pass. PR 6bf2f34.

title: --files flag on discover silently ignored
description:
## Impact

The `--files` flag on `testaruda discover` is accepted by the CLI but has no effect — the discover pipeline always walks the full project tree via `walkdir`.

## Root cause

In `main.rs`, `run_discover_pipeline` assigns the `--files` value to `_delta` (underscore prefix = intentionally unused):

```rust
pub fn run_discover_pipeline(
    store: &testaruda::Store,
    registry: &testaruda::adapter::AdapterRegistry,
    _delta: &testaruda::ChangeSet,  // ← never consulted
) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
```

## Reproduction

```bash
testaruda discover --files src/main.py
# Still discovers all tests, not just those related to main.py
```

## Location
- `main.rs` — `run_discover_pipeline` function signature
- CLI argument definition for `--files` on discover

## Action
Either:
1. Make `--files` actually scope discovery (pass file paths to adapter's discover, or filter results server-side)
2. Remove the `--files` flag from discover to avoid misleading users

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--files` flag either works or is removed from discover help
- [ ] If kept, passing file paths scopes discovery to relevant tests only

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — DRAFT-002.
close_reason: Removed --files flag from discover command. Also removed unused _delta parameter from run_discover_pipeline. All 107 tests pass. PR aac041b.

description:

title: parse_python_imports doesn'\''t handle relative imports
description:
## Impact

The `parse_python_imports` function only handles two patterns at top indentation level:
- `import X` 
- `from X import Y` (absolute imports only)

Not handled:
- `from .module import ...` (relative imports)
- `from ..package import ...`
- Conditional imports inside `try/except`
- Imports inside function bodies
- Dynamic `__import__()` calls

This means the Python adapter misses dependency edges for projects that use relative imports, causing selection to miss real dependencies.

## Location
- `adapter-python.rs` — `parse_python_imports` function

## Action
Use a proper Python import parser (stdlib `ast` module with a Rust binding, or a lightweight regex that handles relative imports) rather than line-based string parsing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Relative imports (`from .module import ...`) are detected
- [ ] Package-relative imports (`from ..package import ...`) are detected
- [ ] Top-level imports continue to work
- [ ] Test suite passes

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 4.
design: Replace line-based string parsing with a solution that handles relative imports (from .module import ...), package-relative imports (from ..package import ...), conditional imports inside try/except, and imports inside function bodies. Approaches include: (a) Rust binding to Python stdlib ast module, (b) lightweight regex that handles dotted relative paths, (c) custom recursive descent parser. The chosen approach must not regress existing absolute import detection.
close_reason: Closed

title: CLI ingest and adapter ingest protocols are disconnected
description:
## Impact

The CLI `ingest` command and the adapter-level `ingest` command are disconnected. The CLI ingest goes directly to `Store::ingest()` and never calls the adapter's ingest. Adapter-level ingest produces `per_test_results` and `runtime_edges`, but there is no path to propagate those into the store's dependency graph.

## Details

- The Python adapter has its own `ingest` command (separate from CLI `testaruda ingest`)
- Adapter ingest accepts `params.run_output` as raw string and parses pytest verbose output for PASSED/FAILED
- Adapter ingest returns `runtime_edges: []` (always empty — `capabilities.runtime_edges: false` in handshake)
- CLI ingest takes a JSON file with `run_id` + `tests` array, calls `Store::ingest()` directly

## Location
- `store.rs` — `Store::ingest()` 
- `adapter-python.rs` — `cmd_ingest`
- `main.rs` — CLI ingest command handler

## Action
Either:
1. (Preferred) Have the CLI ingest delegate to the adapter's ingest and use returned data to populate edges
2. Document the gap clearly and mark adapter-level ingest as deprecated

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CLI ingest produces runtime dependency edges from test runner output
- [ ] Either ingest path works correctly

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 3a.
design: Decision: Deprecate adapter-level ingest protocol and remove it from the adapter contract. The CLI ingest (Store::ingest()) handles all ingestion directly. Adapter-level ingest should return runtime_edges from coverage data. Path forward: (1) Make adapter ingest return coverage-based runtime edges, (2) Have CLI ingest delegate to adapter ingest via run_adapter_pipeline, (3) Feed returned edges into Store::ingest().
acceptance_criteria: Adapter-level ingest returns runtime_edges from parsed coverage output. CLI ingest delegates to adapter ingest before calling Store::ingest(). Runtime edges are persisted in the store. Existing idempotent ingestion behaviour preserved.
close_reason: Closed

title: --agent output lacks node_id and fallback_reason fields
description:
## Impact

The `--agent` output format provides numeric test IDs but no `node_id` (file path), making it hard for agents to map results back to test files without a separate `graph` query. Additionally, when edges are missing (common in v0.1.0), every test shows `always_run: true` with empty `reason_chain`, making it impossible to distinguish "proven affected" from "couldn't prove safe, run everything."

## Details

Current `--agent` output per test:
```json
{ "id": 42, "always_run": true, "reason_chain": [] }
```

Needed:
```json
{ "id": 42, "node_id": "tests/test_model.py", "always_run": true, "fallback_reason": "no edge data available", "reason_chain": [] }
```

## Location
- `main.rs` — agent output format generation

## Action
Add `node_id` (file path) and `fallback_reason` (why test is in always_run state) to agent output.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `--agent` output includes `node_id` for each test
- [ ] `--agent` output includes `fallback_reason` explaining always_run state
- [ ] Output remains parseable as JSON

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 5.
notes: Spec reference: openspec change add-agent-output-fields (MODIFIES TIA-AGENT-001). This change adds node_id and fallback_reason per-test fields to the agent output format.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement idempotent ingestion with run-identity key (TIA-RUN-005)
description:

title: Implement deterministic ordering and agent output (TIA-SEL-005, TIA-AGENT-001..007)
description:
## Part 1: Deterministic selection ordering (this issue)

Implement stable, reproducible ordering of affected test sets. This is the prerequisite for agent output format and CI exit codes.

- Byte-stable output for identical inputs and store state (TIA-SEL-005)
- Default deterministic mode for agent/gate use (TIA-AGENT-007)
- Duration ordering option: descending by recorded mean duration (TIA-SEL-006)
- Predictive ranking constraints: order-only, never remove always-run members (TIA-SEL-007)

close_reason: Implemented deterministic ordering (TIA-SEL-005), duration-based sort (TIA-SEL-006), and predictive ranking constraint (TIA-SEL-007). Added TestOrdering enum, select_with_ordering API, load_mean_durations store method, and comprehensive tests.

title: Implement confidence floor and gating (TIA-CONF-002, TIA-SAFE-002..003)
description:
Implement the per-invocation confidence floor from coverage freshness, adapter resolution, history depth, and environment match. Wire confidence threshold to component-scoped fallback selecting all tests when below threshold.

Note: Fallback is scoped per affected component. Always-run-only components skip fallback (TIA-SAFE-002 second clause). Depends on adapter protocol (testaruda-9uw) for adapter resolution ratio.

Spec: `openspec/specs/confidence-scoring/spec.md`, `openspec/specs/safety/spec.md`
Contracts: `.espectacular/confidence-scoring/*.toml` (4 contracts), `.espectacular/safety/confidence-below-threshold.toml`, `.espectacular/safety/component-scoped-fallback.toml`, `.espectacular/safety/always-run-only-component.toml`
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Coverage freshness, adapter resolution, history depth, environment match all factored into confidence
- [x] Confidence below threshold → component-scoped full run fallback
- [x] Always-run-only component → no fallback triggered
- [x] Stored edge weights unchanged by invocation-level signals
- [x] Confidence reported in all consumer output formats
- [x] `cargo test` passes

title: Configurable discover exclusion list in testaruda.toml
description:
## Impact

After the hardcoded exclusion fix (testaruda-6j0), the exclude list is baked into the code. Users with non-standard venv paths or custom build directories cannot configure discover to skip them.

## Action

Add a `[discover]` section to `testaruda.toml` with an `exclude` list. The adapter discover walk and engine-level pipeline SHALL skip directories matching any pattern in the list.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] testaruda.toml supports [discover] section with exclude list
- [ ] Discover walk skips all directories matching exclude patterns
- [ ] Engine-level pipeline also applies exclude patterns
- [ ] Default exclude list matches common patterns from testaruda-6j0
- [ ] User can extend or replace default exclude patterns

## Discovery
Split from testaruda-6j0 during issue-review pass. testaruda-6j0 is the hardcoded bug fix (P1); this is the configurable follow-up (P3 feature).

title: init should auto-detect project language
description:
## Impact

On a Python-only project, `testaruda discover` runs the default (Rust) adapter and finds 0 tests. The user must manually edit `testaruda.toml` to change `default = "testaruda-adapter-python"`.

This creates a poor first-run experience and requires reading docs to discover the workaround.

## Suggested approach

Have `init` auto-detect the project language (check for `pyproject.toml` vs `Cargo.toml`), or default to the first configured adapter alphabetically rather than hard-coding `testaruda-adapter-rust`.

## Location
- `main.rs` — `init` command handler
- Config generation in `store.rs` or CLI

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `init` detects Python projects (presence of `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`)
- [ ] `init` detects Rust projects (presence of `Cargo.toml`)
- [ ] Default adapter matches detected language
- [ ] Works for mixed-language projects

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 1.
notes: Spec reference: openspec change add-init-language-detection (ADDS TIA-CHG-009). Specifies init-time probing for pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, etc. to determine default adapter.

title: --json and --pre-edit flags conflict silently
description:
## Impact

The `--json` and `--pre-edit` flags on `select` cannot be combined, but the CLI doesn't validate this. Using both produces confusing/invalid output instead of a clear error message.

## Location
- `main.rs` — CLI argument handling for `select` command

## Action
Add mutual exclusion validation between `--json` and `--pre-edit` flags. Return a clear error message if both are provided.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Using `--json` and `--pre-edit` together produces an error message
- [ ] Each flag works independently
- [ ] Help text mentions mutual exclusivity

## Discovery
Found via testaruda usage report (2026-07-14) — Section 5.

title: Predictive ranking for test ordering (TIA-SEL-007, TIA-VER-005)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-SEL-007 from `openspec/specs/selection-engine/spec.md` and TIA-VER-005 from `openspec/specs/verification/spec.md`:

- **SEL-007** — Predictive ranking: order selected tests by predicted failure likelihood
- **VER-005** — Ranking calibration gate: hold-out evaluation before promoting ranking model

Currently only deterministic (test ID) and duration-based ordering are implemented (SEL-005, SEL-006).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Predictive ranking model interface defined
- [ ] Training data collected from run history
- [ ] Basic frequency-based ranking (order by historical failure rate)
- [ ] Calibration gate with recall targets
notes: Coordinate output format with testaruda-zot (adds node_id and fallback_reason to agent output). If agent format changes, ranking output should use the same schema.

title: CI result ingestion (TIA-CI-008)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-CI-008 from `openspec/specs/ci-integration/spec.md`:

- **CI-008** — Result ingestion: CI mode automatically ingests test results after running selected tests

Currently, `testaruda ingest` is a separate manual step. CI-008 would make it automatic after the test run.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `testaruda select --ci` optionally runs tests and ingests results
- [ ] Test runner output is captured and fed to ingest automatically
- [ ] Exit codes reflect post-ingestion state

title: Flaky test detection and exclusion (TIA-SAFE-011, TIA-SAFE-012)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-SAFE-011 and TIA-SAFE-012 from `openspec/specs/safety/spec.md`:

- **SAFE-011** — Flaky detection: identify tests whose outcomes oscillate between passed/failed across runs on the same selection
- **SAFE-012** — Flaky exclusion from training: exclude flaky test outcomes from confidence scoring

The store schema already accepts `flaky` as an outcome value — detection logic is what's missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Flaky detection heuristic implemented (e.g., N retries, outcome oscillation tracking)
- [ ] Flaky tests excluded from confidence model
- [ ] Flaky status surfaced in agent output and explain

title: Observability: metrics emission and structured logs (TIA-OBS-003, TIA-OBS-004)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-OBS-003 and TIA-OBS-004 from `openspec/specs/observability/spec.md`:

- **OBS-003** — Metrics emission: emit counters and histograms for selection latency, test counts, confidence distribution
- **OBS-004** — Structured logs: machine-parseable log output with consistent fields

OBS-001 (graph export) and OBS-002 (selection explanation) are already implemented.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Basic metrics emitted during selection (counts, latency)
- [ ] Structured log output with JSON format
- [ ] Configurable log level

title: Local mode: daemon, watch, rerun (TIA-LOCAL-001..005)
description:
## Requirements

TIA-LOCAL-001..005 from `openspec/specs/local-mode/spec.md`:

- **LOCAL-001** — Working tree selection: `select` uses the local working tree as change source when no base/head revisions are given
- **LOCAL-002** — Daemon mode: background process that caches state across invocations
- **LOCAL-003** — Watch mode: file-system watcher that re-runs selection on change
- **LOCAL-004** — Local failure rerun: re-run only failed tests from last local run
- **LOCAL-005** — Offline operation: no external dependencies required

## Dependencies

Depends on core selection pipeline (implemented in v0.2.0).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `testaruda select` with no args works on working tree
- [ ] Daemon mode specification written
- [ ] Watch mode specification written
- [ ] Design doc for local workflow

title: fix: justfile parse error (I6 regression)
notes:
The justfile had a Markdown/HTML boilerplate block prepended above the real recipes, preventing just from parsing it. This blocked all just recipes including `just test`, `just build`, `just check`, and `just ah`.

Root cause: Markdown fenced code blocks and HTML comments accidentally committed into the recipe file.

Fix applied (https://github.com/charly/testaruda/commit/WIP): Replaced the Markdown preamble with 16 proper just recipes and removed all non-just content.

Verification:
- `just --list` shows 16 available recipes
- `just build` compiles successfully

Closes: I6 from the testaruda evaluation, and Backlog gap B (§8.4).
close_reason: Fixed: replaced Markdown preamble with proper justfile recipes. 16 recipes available, just build passes.
